Abstract
    

The cycle double cover conjecture of Szekeres and Seymour, the proof of which was recently announced
by OpenAI, states that every bridgeless graph has a collection of cycles
covering every edge exactly twice.
We study the counting version of this statement for cubic graphs, where we count circuit double covers —
collections of circuits (connected 2-regular subgraphs) covering every edge
twice. We show that every 2-edge-connected 3-edge-colorable cubic graph on nn
vertices has at least 2n/2−12^{n/2-1} circuit double covers, matching our
previously conjectured general lower bound.
For every 3-edge-connected cubic graph with girth at least 16 we show a weaker
exponential lower bound on circuit double covers.
For both of these results we use the same system of linear equations used by OpenAI in their proof,
however, we provide additional combinatorial interpretation.
We characterize planarity of a cubic graph by solvability of this system of equations for arbitrary nowhere-zero ℤ2k\mathbb{Z}_{2}^{k}-flow.
We give a condition on the flow that is equivalent to existence of a 5-cycle double cover.

1 Introduction




We consider undirected connected graphs. The graph is usually denoted GG with
VV being the set of its vertices and EE the set of its edges.
We consider simple cubic (i.e., 3-regular) graphs unless noted otherwise.
Loops and multiedges are not interesting as they
force existence of a 1-cut or 2-cut unless the connected component
is just three parallel edges.
Throughout, connectivity and cuts refer to edge-connectivity and edge-cuts unless explicitly stated otherwise.
However, for cubic graphs, the edge and vertex connectivity coincide.




We denote by E⁡(v)E(v) the set of edges incident with vertex vv.
We write [A→B][A\to B] for the set of all functions from AA to BB.
We will use flows throughout the paper but always only ℤ2k\mathbb{Z}_{2}^{k}-flows,
so we do not need directed edges. Note that we always treat ℤ2k\mathbb{Z}_{2}^{k}
as a kk-dimensional space over ℤ2\mathbb{Z}_{2}.



Definition 1.1 (Flow).



A mapping f:E→ℤ2kf:E\to\mathbb{Z}_{2}^{k} is a ℤ2k\mathbb{Z}_{2}^{k}-flow if ∑e∈E⁡(v)f⁡(e)=0\sum_{e\in E(v)}f(e)=0 for
all v∈Vv\in V. We say that a flow ff is nowhere-zero (or NZ for short)
if f⁡(e)≠0f(e)\neq 0 for all e∈Ee\in E.

          As of
July 2026 the proof has not yet appeared in a refereed publication, but it is
accompanied by a Lean formalization [OAIb].
An exposition by Oum [Oum] adds more explanations to the proof.
We present another point of view on the proof announced by OpenAI and extend it in several ways,
mostly involving counting.
First, we prove Corollary 3.8, that gives Ω⁡(2n/2)\Omega(2^{n/2}) 8-CyDCs by
only noting that 8-CyDCs bijectively correspond to solutions of the system of linear equations (2).
We also show the following linear algebraic planarity characterization.



Theorem 1.6.



Let GG be a 2-edge-connected cubic graph. Then GG is planar if and only if system (2)
is solvable for every nowhere-zero ℤ25\mathbb{Z}_{2}^{5}-flow on GG. If GG is 3-edge-colorable,
ℤ25\mathbb{Z}_{2}^{5} may be replaced by ℤ24\mathbb{Z}_{2}^{4}.





For 3-edge-colorable cubic graphs (where existence of a CiDC is well-known), we prove
a bound on their number matching Conjecture 1.5.



Theorem 1.7.



Let GG be a 2-connected 3-edge-colorable cubic graph on nn vertices.
Then GG has at least 2n/2−12^{n/2-1} CiDCs.





In [HS] we observed the result is tight for so-called Klee graphs. In [HS] we showed that the minimal counterexample to Conjecture 1.5
does not have nontrivial cut smaller than 4 and does not have 4-cycles.
Here, we prove that graphs with high enough girth have exponentially many CiDCs.
